entries.cuda_mechanism: cudaMalloc + cudaMemcpy H2D/D2H around every kernel
entries.why_it_exists: a discrete GPU has its own physical memory the CPU cannot address
entries.underlying_problem: data must physically cross PCIe to be computed on
entries.apple_equivalent: none needed; CPU and GPU address the same physical memory
entries.hawking_equivalent: cuda_runtime.execute_host UNIFIED mode: cudaMalloc becomes an alias and both cudaMemcpy directions become no-ops, guarded by may_delete_copies()

performance_gap.value: eliminating the copies is worth 7.4x on the copy itself (P6 microbenchmark) and 1.7x inside a translated host program

entries.test_corpus: vadd and vmul host programs at 4096 and 2^22 in both modes, plus a hazard program that writes its host buffer between the copy and the launch
entries.current_winner: Hawking resident-operand path
entries.remaining_limitation: THE DELETION IS CONDITIONAL, and calling this gap deleted without the condition would be wrong. A CUDA host-to-device copy is a SNAPSHOT; an alias is a LIVE REFERENCE. A program that writes the host buffer after the copy and before the launch DIVERGES -- demonstrated at 999.36 in exactly one element with every other element bit-identical. may_delete_copies() refuses those programs by name. Also unhandled: device-to-device copies, async copies, pinned and managed memory, all refused rather than emulated.

entries.cuda_mechanism: dequantize to dense then call cuBLAS, or a fused dequant-GEMM kernel
entries.why_it_exists: tensor cores consume dense formats; compact formats must be expanded
entries.underlying_problem: compact weights are not directly consumable by library GEMM
entries.apple_equivalent: none provided; MLX quantized ops cover its own formats only
entries.hawking_equivalent: representation-native matvec reading packed nibbles + f16 group scales

performance_gap.value: no advantage below ~64 MiB; 2.08x at 256 MiB where it becomes bandwidth-bound

entries.test_corpus: real Qwen3-30B-A3B expert tensor at ws_rtn_q4_g64
entries.current_winner: Hawking native kernel above the crossover; nothing below it
entries.remaining_limitation: matvec only; no GEMM, no batched form, and one expert sits BELOW the crossover so single-expert use gains nothing

entries.cuda_mechanism: hand-fused kernels, or a compiler like Triton/torch.compile
entries.why_it_exists: each launch re-reads and re-writes memory an op chain need not touch
entries.underlying_problem: unfused chains are bandwidth-bound on intermediates
entries.apple_equivalent: MLX does not fuse an arbitrary elementwise chain automatically
entries.hawking_equivalent: AIR lowers a multi-op SSA chain into one kernel

performance_gap.value: 1.71x over the naive 3-kernel translation, 2.62x over MLX

entries.test_corpus: mul->relu->silu chain, 2^24 f32
entries.current_winner: Hawking fused AIR program
entries.remaining_limitation: elementwise chains over one shape and dtype only

entries.cuda_mechanism: NVRTC / driver JIT of PTX at runtime
entries.why_it_exists: shapes and constants are not known until run time
entries.underlying_problem: AOT compilation cannot specialise on runtime values
entries.apple_equivalent: Metal runtime library compilation; MLX exposes it via metal_kernel
entries.hawking_equivalent: AIR emits MSL, MLX JIT-compiles it

performance_gap.value: 36.8 ms per DISTINCT kernel on this machine, near-flat in source size (102 chars 36.8 ms, 5990 chars 43.6 ms) and CACHED on repeat: the same name+source recompiles in 0.24 ms. Compile is 23.2% of a WorkUnit's first-run excess; MLX's own first-use costs are 55.1%, dominated by the FIRST mx.array at 151 ms, which is device/allocator init and NOT compilation.

entries.test_corpus: the six AIR programs of P3
entries.current_winner: MLX JIT (retained; nothing here replaces it)
entries.remaining_limitation: measured on mx.fast.metal_kernel JIT only; xcrun metal AOT is ABSENT on this machine so an AOT metallib comparison cannot be made, and CUDA's own nvrtc latency is unmeasured because no NVIDIA hardware exists

entries.cuda_mechanism: template parameters and __constant__ values baked at compile time
entries.why_it_exists: a constant known at compile time removes a load and enables unrolling
entries.underlying_problem: runtime values block optimisation
entries.apple_equivalent: Metal function constants
entries.hawking_equivalent: AirProgram.specialization emits const floats into the MSL

performance_gap.value: NO MEASURABLE BENEFIT on this backend. A literal scalar against a buffer read is INDISTINGUISHABLE (1.62% margin vs 7.95% noise); a compute-bound loop bound where unrolling should pay is INDISTINGUISHABLE with the literal 3.09% SLOWER, both arms clean at 5.25%/4.96%.

entries.test_corpus: saxpy->relu with ALPHA as a specialization constant
entries.current_winner: UNKNOWN — never measured against a non-specialised variant
entries.remaining_limitation: two shapes on one machine; whether the literal loop is actually unrolled cannot be checked because xcrun metal is ABSENT so generated code cannot be inspected; and a constant that would enable BRANCH ELIMINATION or a different memory layout is untested

entries.cuda_mechanism: blockIdx/blockDim/threadIdx and the launch configuration
entries.why_it_exists: a portable way to index a data-parallel launch
entries.underlying_problem: mapping work onto a hierarchy of parallel units
entries.apple_equivalent: thread_position_in_grid and threadgroup sizing
entries.hawking_equivalent: C2M recognises the canonical global index and maps it
entries.test_corpus: the four translated kernels of P4
entries.current_winner: Hawking C2M for the canonical form
entries.remaining_limitation: ONLY the 1-D canonical form; no 2-D or 3-D grids, no block-relative indexing, no grid-stride loops

entries.cuda_mechanism: __shared__ arrays with block-scoped lifetime
entries.why_it_exists: a software-managed scratchpad far faster than global memory
entries.underlying_problem: reuse within a block should not go to DRAM
entries.apple_equivalent: threadgroup address space
entries.hawking_equivalent: tools/accelerator/gemm.py tiled GEMM

performance_gap.value: MLX 12733 GFLOP/s vs ours 2683 at 2048^2 = 4.7x in MLX's favour

entries.test_corpus: 512/1024/2048 square f32 GEMM vs MLX, plus 2 negative controls
entries.current_winner: MLX, retained (§141) -- replacement is not justified by evidence
entries.remaining_limitation: threadgroup tiles execute; no double buffering, no bank-conflict work

entries.cuda_mechanism: atomicAdd/atomicCAS on global and shared memory
entries.why_it_exists: concurrent accumulation without a separate reduction pass
entries.underlying_problem: many threads updating one location
entries.apple_equivalent: atomic_fetch_add_explicit in MSL
entries.hawking_equivalent: atomic_fetch_add_explicit in AIR's atomic reduction strategy

performance_gap.value: single-pass atomic sum is 3.05x/1.80x over two-stage; INDISTINGUISHABLE from MLX

entries.test_corpus: sum at 2^20 and 2^24, atomic vs two-stage vs MLX, plus a refusal for max
entries.current_winner: MLX and AIR indistinguishable; MLX retained as incumbent
entries.remaining_limitation: float ADD only. No atomic max (Metal lacks it here, so the strategy refuses), no CAS, no integer atomics, no shared-memory atomics. Summation order is NONDETERMINISTIC and the result is 3.4x less exact than the two-stage form.

entries.cuda_mechanism: __shfl_sync, __ballot_sync, warp-level reduction
entries.why_it_exists: intra-warp exchange without shared memory or barriers
entries.underlying_problem: lane-to-lane communication inside a scheduling unit
entries.apple_equivalent: simd_shuffle and friends over a 32-wide SIMD group
entries.hawking_equivalent: simdgroup_float8x8 matrix ops in AIR's simdgroup matmul strategy

performance_gap.value: 1.6x over a scalar tile; 91-98% of MLX at 512/1024 but 36.7% at 2048

entries.test_corpus: 512/1024/2048 f32 GEMM, simdgroup vs tiled vs MLX
entries.current_winner: MLX, retained
entries.remaining_limitation: simdgroup MATRIX ops work; shuffle, ballot and vote are still untouched, and Apple's divergence semantics remain uncompared to CUDA's

entries.cuda_mechanism: __syncthreads and cooperative groups
entries.why_it_exists: phase separation inside a block
entries.underlying_problem: ordering between cooperating threads
entries.apple_equivalent: threadgroup_barrier
entries.hawking_equivalent: tools/accelerator/gemm.py tiled GEMM

performance_gap.value: MLX 12733 GFLOP/s vs ours 2683 at 2048^2 = 4.7x in MLX's favour

entries.test_corpus: 512/1024/2048 square f32 GEMM vs MLX, plus 2 negative controls
entries.current_winner: MLX, retained (§141) -- replacement is not justified by evidence
entries.remaining_limitation: threadgroup_barrier executes; SIMDGROUP and DEVICE scope untested, and AIR can represent a barrier but cannot lower one

entries.cuda_mechanism: cuBLAS GEMM on tensor cores
entries.why_it_exists: matrix multiply is the dominant cost of a transformer
entries.underlying_problem: peak arithmetic needs tiling, blocking and hardware MMA units
entries.apple_equivalent: MLX matmul; Apple matrix coprocessor via MPS
entries.hawking_equivalent: AIR simdgroup matmul with 2x2 register blocking

performance_gap.value: parity with MLX at 1024 and 2048; MLX wins 1.24x at 4096

entries.test_corpus: 512/1024/2048 square f32 GEMM vs MLX, plus 2 negative controls
entries.current_winner: MLX at 4096 and above; parity below, so MLX is retained
entries.remaining_limitation: parity to 2048, then MLX pulls ahead 1.24x at 4096; no threadgroup-level staging, no double buffering, no batching, no transpose, f32 only

entries.cuda_mechanism: CUB block/device reduce and scan
entries.why_it_exists: reductions are latency-critical and hard to write well
entries.underlying_problem: tree reduction across a hierarchy with correct synchronization
entries.apple_equivalent: MLX reductions; simd_sum
entries.hawking_equivalent: AIR two-stage reduction (sum, max) and three-phase scan (sum, max) with two strategies each

performance_gap.value: scan beats mx.cumsum 8.09x at 2^24 and 1.84x at 2^20; reduction loses 1.75x to mx.sum at 2^24 and is not distinguishable at 2^20. The earlier 'atomics win 3.05x on launch count' is REFUTED -- the cost was host round trips, not launches.

entries.test_corpus: sum/max reduce and inclusive/exclusive/max scan at 7, 256, 1000, non-power-of-two 4099, 2^16, 2^20, 2^22, 2^24, graded against an f64 oracle and cross-checked against mx.cumsum
entries.current_winner: SPLIT: Hawking for scan (mx.cumsum runs at 19 GB/s on a 589 GB/s machine here); MLX for reduction, retained
entries.remaining_limitation: f32 only, 1-D only. Scan is sum and max; exclusive is sum-only (derived as inclusive minus x) and the simd_prefix strategy is sum-only because Metal has no prefix max. No segmented scan, no scan-by-key, no multi-dimensional or strided axis. Nothing here has run inside a model.

entries.cuda_mechanism: cudaStream_t, cudaEvent_t, async launch and dependency ordering
entries.why_it_exists: overlap of compute and transfer, and explicit dependency expression
entries.underlying_problem: serialising independent work wastes the device
entries.apple_equivalent: MTLCommandQueue, command buffers, MTLEvent
entries.hawking_equivalent: AirGraph expresses independence as DAG width; there are no named streams and no events

performance_gap.value: independent branches overlap only weakly: 1.09x at k=8 and 1.16x at k=16 over a serial chain of the same work at 2^20, and NO_CLAIM at 4096. Concurrency is the SMALLER half of what a graph buys here

entries.test_corpus: fan (depth 1, width k) vs chain (depth k, width 1), same total work
entries.current_winner: MLX's own scheduling, retained; we do not control it
entries.remaining_limitation: No named streams, no events, no cross-stream dependencies, no host callbacks, no priority. Only DAG width is expressed, and the runtime decides what to do with it.

entries.cuda_mechanism: CUDA Graphs: capture once, replay with minimal launch overhead
entries.why_it_exists: per-launch CPU cost dominates short kernels in a tight loop
entries.underlying_problem: re-encoding an unchanged command stream every iteration
entries.apple_equivalent: indirect command buffers; reusable command buffers
entries.hawking_equivalent: AIR AirGraph: a recorded dependency DAG executed as one command-buffer submission with one host sync

performance_gap.value: batching k dispatches into one submission cuts the marginal cost of an added dispatch 15.5x (0.168 -> 0.011 ms); total 2.9x at k=4, 4.8x at k=8, 8.0x at k=16

entries.test_corpus: chain and fan of k=1,2,4,8,16 elementwise dispatches at 4096 and 2^20
entries.current_winner: Hawking AirGraph (MLX's laziness supplies the batching; AirGraph makes it explicit and measurable)
entries.remaining_limitation: No graph instantiation or update reuse, no conditional or dynamic nodes, no cross-device nodes. The DAG is re-recorded per call; only the compiled kernels are cached.

entries.cuda_mechanism: cudaEventElapsedTime, Nsight Compute counters
entries.why_it_exists: optimisation without measurement is guessing
entries.underlying_problem: attributing time to a specific kernel on an async device
entries.apple_equivalent: Metal GPU counters; Instruments
entries.hawking_equivalent: bench.py wall-clock with warmup, IQR gate and an implausibility rejection

performance_gap.reason: the instrument is not itself benchmarked

entries.test_corpus: every timed arm in P5, P6, P7
entries.current_winner: Hawking bench.py for comparisons
entries.remaining_limitation: WALL CLOCK ONLY — no DRAM byte counters, no occupancy, no stall reasons, so mechanism is inferred rather than observed

entries.cuda_mechanism: compute-sanitizer, device printf, cuda-gdb
entries.why_it_exists: silent numerical corruption is the worst failure mode
entries.underlying_problem: a wrong answer at speed looks like a right answer
entries.apple_equivalent: Metal shader validation, GPU frame capture
entries.hawking_equivalent: every candidate verified against an oracle BEFORE it is timed
entries.test_corpus: P3 six programs, P4 four kernels, forge 15 variants
entries.current_winner: Hawking verify-before-time discipline
entries.remaining_limitation: oracle comparison only; no race detection, no OOB checking, no device-side assertion

entries.cuda_mechanism: cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess, NVLink, NCCL collectives
entries.why_it_exists: multi-GPU training and inference need direct device-to-device paths
entries.underlying_problem: moving tensors between devices without a host bounce
entries.apple_equivalent: none on a single SoC; Thunderbolt/RDMA between machines
entries.hawking_equivalent: HUMF models the domains but only a MOCK external one exists

performance_gap.reason: no real second device exists; every transport number so far is SIMULATED and may not be cited as evidence

entries.test_corpus: HUMF P8 across APPLE_UM and MOCK_EXTERNAL_VRAM
entries.current_winner: NOT APPLICABLE — no second physical device
entries.remaining_limitation: EGB-D0 has not been reached; no hardware is present

entries.cuda_mechanism: hand-fused softmax kernels, or cuDNN's
entries.why_it_exists: softmax is on the critical path of every attention layer and is bandwidth-bound, so its passes over memory dominate
entries.underlying_problem: three dependent reductions over the same row, naively three passes
entries.apple_equivalent: mx.softmax
entries.hawking_equivalent: AIR fused row softmax, one threadgroup per row, two barriers

performance_gap.value: 1.46x/1.35x over the naive three-pass shape; INDISTINGUISHABLE from MLX

entries.test_corpus: 64x128, 512x1024, 128x4099, 8x3, an overflow row, and a barrier-stripped negative control
entries.current_winner: MLX and AIR are indistinguishable; MLX retained as incumbent
entries.remaining_limitation: f32 only, last axis only, no masking, no causal variant. ATTENTION ITSELF REMAINS ABSENT -- this is a piece of it.

entries.cuda_mechanism: FlashAttention and cuDNN fused attention kernels
entries.why_it_exists: attention materialises an O(seq^2) score matrix that dominates memory traffic and capacity at long sequence
entries.underlying_problem: a chain of matmul, softmax and matmul where the intermediates are far larger than the inputs
entries.apple_equivalent: mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention
entries.hawking_equivalent: AIR fused single-head attention, score row in threadgroup memory

performance_gap.value: loses to naive 1.37x at 1024; a simdgroup rebuild is SLOWER still (0.70x)

entries.test_corpus: 512/1024/2048 with head_dim 64 and 128, a causal variant, a non-power-of-two 37x40, and a refusal case at seq 100000
entries.current_winner: MLX, and at 2048 even the NAIVE three-call path beats ours
entries.remaining_limitation: not flash-attention: no online softmax, score row must fit threadgroup memory. Diagnosis history: 'scalar dot products' REFUTED; 'occupancy' DIRECTIONALLY CONFIRMED -- 4 simdgroups on the same query block take the simdgroup variant from 0.70x losing to INDISTINGUISHABLE from the scalar kernel. But the NAIVE three-MLX-call path STILL WINS 1.08x with clean arms, so fused attention is not useful here at these shapes. Single head, f32, no batching, no KV cache.

entries.cuda_mechanism: nvcc / clang CUDA frontend: a full C++ frontend for device and host code
entries.why_it_exists: CUDA's corpus is written in C++, so a compiler must accept C++
entries.underlying_problem: turning arbitrary source into an executable device program
entries.apple_equivalent: the Metal compiler accepts MSL, a different C++ dialect; nothing accepts CUDA
entries.hawking_equivalent: C2M's FOUR narrow doors: T0 expression matching over 4 elementwise forms, a PTX instruction subset, the T1 host runtime statement subset, and T2 algorithm-level IDIOM RECOGNITION over 2 kernels

performance_gap.reason: a frontend gap is about COVERAGE, not speed; measuring a translation rate would say nothing about how much of CUDA is reachable

entries.test_corpus: 4 elementwise kernels, the pinned seed's 291 .ptx files, 4 host programs, 2 recognised idioms and 12 near-miss kernels
entries.current_winner: the pinned seed Lulzx/cuda-metal, which has a REAL clang-based CUDA frontend and builds here; C2M does not compete with it on coverage and is not claimed to
entries.remaining_limitation: THIS IS THE LARGEST REMAINING SOFTWARE GAP AND IT IS NOT NARROWING QUICKLY. None of the four doors parses C++. PTX coverage measured 1.0% of the seed's own corpus. Idiom recognition covers exactly 2 textbook kernels and REFUSES the same algorithm written with different variable names or a different guard style. Adding doors widens what is reachable without widening what is COMPILABLE, and saying so keeps a tier number from reading as CUDA coverage.

parity_claim: NOT CLAIMED. This is a capability inventory, not a parity statement. No entry may report a semantic gap of NONE without evidence, and the steer forbids the phrase 'CUDA parity' unqualified.
coverage_honesty: The CUDA surface is vastly larger than this. These are the capabilities reachable or relevant from what has actually been built here; absence from this ledger means NOT YET STUDIED, never NOT NEEDED.
